- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75.00), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not exceed 2–3% above recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-adjusted values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment’s 3-period moving average.
